title: Chicken Parmigiana with Spaghetti
summary: Crumbed chicken cutlets are fried until golden, topped with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella, then served over spaghetti.
equipment: rimmed baking tray with a rack

ingredients.item: large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 300 g each), halved horizontally into 4 cutlets
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt, only if needed
ingredients.note: about 1 pinch; taste first: tinned tomatoes are usually salted

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for the pasta water (7.5 g in 1.5 litres, 0.5%)

steps.title: Simmer the tomato sauce
steps.text: Warm the olive oil and garlic in a saucepan over medium-low heat for 1-2 minutes until pale gold, then add the tomatoes, oregano, salt if needed and a few basil stems. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until thickened, tasting first since tinned tomatoes are usually already salted.

steps.title: Flatten and season the chicken
steps.text: Pound the cutlets between cling film to an even 6 mm thickness, then season with the salt and pepper.

steps.title: Coat the cutlets
steps.text: Dip each cutlet in flour, then beaten egg, then the panko mixed with parmesan, pressing the crumb on firmly so it holds.

steps.title: Fry until golden
steps.text: Heat the oil to about 1 cm deep in the frying pan over medium-high until it reaches around 175°C, hot enough that a crumb sizzles instantly. Fry the cutlets 2 at a time for about 2 minutes per side until deep golden and the centre reaches 74°C, then drain on the rack.

steps.title: Grill with sauce and cheese
steps.text: Heat the grill (broiler) to high. Set the cutlets on the rack-lined tray, spoon 2 tablespoons of sauce onto the centre of each, leaving the crisp edges bare, then top with the mozzarella and parmesan. Grill for 3-4 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling and browned in spots.

steps.title: Cook the pasta and serve
steps.text: While the cutlets grill, cook the spaghetti in 1.5 litres of boiling water salted with 7.5 g (1¼ tsp) salt - a light 0.5% because the sauce and cheese are already salty - for 1 minute less than the packet suggests, then drain and toss with most of the remaining sauce. Serve the cutlets on the spaghetti, scattered with basil.

tips: Leave the outer edges of each cutlet free of sauce and cheese before grilling so they stay crisp rather than turning soggy.
Common mistake: drowning the fried cutlets in sauce. A spoonful in the centre is enough; serve the rest alongside with the pasta.
Check the oil temperature before frying - too cool and the crumb turns greasy rather than crisp.
Pound the chicken to an even thickness so it cooks through at the same rate as the crust browns.
Undercook the pasta slightly before draining, since it will keep softening slightly while you plate up.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Store sauce and cooked cutlets separately in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat cutlets in the oven or under the grill until piping hot (74°C) to keep the crumb crisp; a microwave will make it soggy. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
